areaDescription: Nestled among golden fields and twisting cobblestone lanes, the Pottsfield Hearthlands exude a rustic charm that belies a simmering tension beneath its harvest festivals and lantern-lit porches. Visitors soon sense watchful eyes behind lace-curtained windows and hear the low murmur of secrets carried on the autumn wind.

map.notes: Extended schema with AI-friendly navigation fields

locations.name: Gravebinders' Assembly
locations.description: Once a stone barn, this assembly hall is the headquarters for Pottsfield's secretive undertakers' guild. Rows of rustic benches and faded banners bearing cryptic emblems flank a wide hearth, its embers cold despite the town's chill. Shelves of bone-handled tools and ledgers line the walls. The air carries the scent of old earth and dried rosemary.

npcs.name: Deputy Silas Cragg
npcs.description: A gaunt, sharp-eyed man in a patched uniform, Deputy Silas Cragg acts as the town's unofficial law and the Gravebinders' chief enforcer. He is ever-watchful, wary of strangers, and harbors deep suspicions of anyone poking into the town’s affairs. Cragg is terse, but may offer wary cooperation if convinced the party means no harm.
npcs.attitude: Guarded, stern; will question the party's intentions and warn them against 'disturbing the peace'.

lootTable: Set of bone-handled grave tools (set, 5 gp)
Ledger listing names and odd symbols (clue)
Phial of gravebloom oil (10 gp, faintly magical, necromancy)
plotHooks: A cryptic ledger hints at townsfolk who died but were seen alive later.
Deputy Cragg warns of trespassers in the Parish Grounds vanishing without a trace.
A locked chest beneath the hearth is rumored to contain forbidden rites.
locations.dmInstructions: Deputy Silas Cragg should question the party; if they seek information about recent disappearances or the town’s strange custom, a DC 13 Persuasion check can soften his attitude. The ledger is a major clue. Combat is unlikely unless the party acts with clear hostility or tries to steal guild secrets.

doors.name: Main Hall Door
doors.description: Heavy oak double doors, weathered and creaking on iron hinges.

doors.name: Hearth Trapdoor
doors.description: Concealed beneath the hearth's ashes, a sturdy trapdoor with a brass ring.

dcChecks: Perception DC 13: Notice the faint outline of the hearth trapdoor.
Investigation DC 15: Decipher the ledger's coded entries.
locations.accessibility: Normal access during daylight; after dusk, only guild members can enter without raising suspicion.

features.name: Dust
features.description: A heavy mantle of undisturbed dust covers ledgers and benches, except the hearth area—recently disturbed.

features.name: Guild Emblems
features.description: Faded banners display a scythe entwined with a lantern—symbol of the Gravebinders.

encounters: Deputy Silas Cragg interrogates the party about their purpose.
A hidden chest (DC 15 Perception) contains ritual scrolls (see loot).
locations.adventureSummary: The party may gain critical information about Pottsfield’s necromantic secrets and the guild’s true role if they earn Cragg's trust or search the room.

locations.name: Shrouded Barrow Gate
locations.description: A wrought-iron archway crowned with carved pumpkin lanterns—some lit, some cold—marks the entrance to Pottsfield’s oldest burial grounds. A low, crumbling stone wall surrounds the gardens beyond. Fine mist lingers in the morning, thickening at dusk. The gate’s hinges groan under the weight of years, and a faint chill seeps from beyond.

npcs.name: Widow Elsie Tallow
npcs.description: A gaunt, veiled woman in black, tending a lantern and muttering prayers for the dead. She is both gatekeeper and mourner, fiercely protective of the grounds. Elsie knows much about Pottsfield’s secret rites, but is haunted by memories of loved ones lost (and returned).
npcs.attitude: Distrustful of outsiders but softened by genuine grief; will warn the party about disturbing the graves.

lootTable: Iron gate key (worn by Widow Tallow)
Prayer beads carved from pumpkin seed (arcane focus, minor)
plotHooks: Widow Tallow reveals people sometimes leave the cemetery 'different' than they entered.
The lanterns' flames flicker seemingly in response to unspoken questions.
A hidden inscription on the archway hints at a ritual to appease restless spirits.
locations.dmInstructions: Widow Tallow should be roleplayed with deep sorrow and suspicion. The area is a threshold to the Parish Grounds (PPG001); she will reluctantly allow respectful adventurers to pass if convinced of their good intentions (DC 12 Persuasion, advantage if they share a story of loss). After sunset, spirits may manifest beyond the gate.

doors.name: Iron Barrow Gate
doors.description: Tall iron-barred gate, decorated with corroded pumpkin lanterns and curling vines.

traps.damage: None; a silent bell alerts the Gravebinders if tampered with.

dcChecks: Religion DC 10: Recognize the lanterns as symbols of warding against undeath.
Investigation DC 14: Find the hidden inscription on the archway.
locations.accessibility: Normally locked after sundown; daytime access permitted if a mourner or guild member is present.

features.name: Interesting Architecture
features.description: The archway is inlaid with faintly-glowing runes and pumpkin motifs, blending beauty and foreboding.

features.name: Dust
features.description: A fine white dust covers the path beyond the gate, disturbed only by fresh footprints.

encounters: Widow Elsie Tallow questions the party’s motives, offering cryptic advice.
Lantern flames flicker in unnatural patterns, hinting at restless spirits.
locations.adventureSummary: This location serves as the literal and thematic threshold to the town's secrets; respectful negotiation or clever investigation here can open the way to deeper mysteries.

locations.name: Harvestbound Hall
locations.description: This stately building of amber-brick and timber hosts the town’s autumn festivals and council meetings. Long tables, festooned with dried corn husks and faded streamers, fill the main hall. The air smells of cider and old wax. Laughter echoes faintly—even when the room is empty. Portraits of past mayors gaze down from the walls, eyes unsettlingly lifelike.

npcs.name: Masked Reveler
npcs.description: A jovial figure in a patchwork cloak and a carved pumpkin mask, the Masked Reveler is both entertainer and secret-keeper. They organize strange harvest games and encourage newcomers to take part. Beneath their mirth lies a calculating mind, ever watching the crowd for threats to Pottsfield’s order.
npcs.attitude: Cheerful and welcoming, but evasive; tests the party’s intentions with riddles and games before revealing anything of substance.

lootTable: Bottle of spiced cider, 'Blessed of the Harvest'
Scroll of festival rites (contains minor abjuration magic, clue)
plotHooks: The Masked Reveler invites the party to participate in a harvest game with subtle, magical consequences.
A painting on the wall appears to move when observed from the corner of one’s eye.
Winners of certain games are given keys or clues related to the town’s deeper mysteries.
locations.dmInstructions: The Masked Reveler should encourage both roleplay and investigation. Success in festival games (see below) might grant minor magical boons, clues, or the trust of the townsfolk. If the party suspects the hall's enchantments, allow Arcana or Insight checks to uncover the truth behind the festivities.

doors.name: Main Entry
doors.description: Wide double doors, painted with harvest scenes and glowing faintly at night.

doors.name: Council Chamber Door
doors.description: Solid pine door with a silvered leaf motif, leading to a private room.

dcChecks: Insight DC 12: Sense the Masked Reveler’s hidden wariness.
Arcana DC 14: Detect a lingering festival enchantment on the hall.
locations.accessibility: Open to all during daylight and festivals; otherwise, council members or festival organizers must permit entry.

features.name: Dust
features.description: Despite regular use, a layer of dust lingers in the corners, disturbed only during festival nights.

features.name: Interesting Architecture
features.description: Vaulted ceilings and magically-lit lanterns subtly change color with the hour.

encounters: Masked Reveler challenges the party to a riddle or harvest game.
A festival-goer (Desperate Townsfolk, if needed elsewhere) is caught cheating and begs the party for help.
locations.adventureSummary: Winning the Reveler’s games or earning their trust may provide vital clues or magical assistance for uncovering the secrets of Pottsfield.
